newsitem.title: CHINA: China mulls new taxes to curb leaded petrol - paper.
newsitem.headline: China mulls new taxes to curb leaded petrol - paper.

text.p: Chinese authorities are considering new taxes on leaded petrol to curb its output and consumption, the official Economic Daily said on Monday.
Authorities plan to levy an additional six percent consumption tax on 90-octane leaded petrol to make it more expensive than unleaded petrol, the newpaper said.
It did not give the current tax level nor did it say when a decision would be made on whether to impose the new tax.
They also plan a 12 percent consumption tax on 70-octane leaded petrol to limit its production and consumption, it said.
The new taxes would be based on ex-refinery prices, the newspaper said.
China plans to phase out the use of leaded petrol in major cities by 2000 in a bid to ease environmental pollution.
Beijing has already started to limit the sale of leaded petrol and Shanghai is expected to follow suit.
